The city outside the large glass window hums with the distant sound of sirens. dialogue.line: Yeah, this isn't Charlie. You better get back to the future. This isn't some hippie orgy.

The city hums with the faint sound of sirens in the distance. A VW van painted in psychedelic colors pulls into a dimly lit alley. Charles Manson the notorious pulp needs sits in the driver's seat, his piercing eyes reflecting in the rearview mirror. Beside him are his two devoted followers, Sadie and Tepz, who exchange nervous glances.
Whisper almost to himself, tonight. We change the course of history. Tonight we ensure the masterpieces of murder never interrupted.
The van stops. Manson steps out, adjusting his leather jacket. He looks up at the sky where a faint glow flickers, signaling a rip in time.
The room is cluttered with gadgets and timelines mapped across the walls. Charlie, a self-proclaimed time travel consultant, tinkers with a strange device.
Dacey, his reluctant partner, enters, holding a peculiar-looking ray gun. Charlie, the warden gave me this. It's supposed to create positive conditions for someone but negative for everyone else.
Grinning. Oh, this is gonna be fun. Causality is about to get a serious makeover. Serious, it's not a game, Charlie. This could have real consequences.
Sign, relax, Dacey. I've got this under control. Now, where's the fun if you don't bend the rules a little?
Frustrated, you're not even listening. This isn't just about bending rules. It's about people's lives.
Before Dacey can argue further, the lab's computer beats a holographic image of Manson. His face twisted into a smirk. You think you can stop me, Charlie? You think you can rewrite the timeline?
Smirking back, Oh, Manson, you know me too. Well, I'm not here to stop you. I'm here to make it interesting. Interesting you call chaos interesting.
